title: Introduce per-tenant latency-protection and graceful-degradation for mixed-length continuous-batcher
creator: Priya Nair
description: Multiple customers across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments reported spikes in short-request P99 latency during sustained mixed-length workloads. Symptoms: short (<=64 token) requests inflated from ~40ms to 800ms+ intermittently, coinciding with large numbers of long-context (>=8k tokens) flows. Oncall RCA identified three correlated failure modes: 1) admission window accounting allowed unbounded prefetch/admission for long-context flows, starving short flows; 2) KV cache eviction churn caused backend stalls when admission size oscillated; 3) router fallback logic routed to higher-latency model variants unexpectedly under pressure. This ticket implements per-tenant soft latency protection and a graceful-degradation path so short requests retain SLO during mixed waves. The fix must work in Hosted (multi-tenant), Dedicated (reserved pools) and Private (customer-managed) topologies and must be reversible without data-plane restarts.
technical_approach: Add per-tenant soft admission quotas enforced in the scheduler: short-request quota and long-request quota with time-decaying tokens
Tag requests at ingress with length-class and tenant-id; expose tag to batcher and admission logic
Introduce 'shortflow-preserve' admission path that reserves a fraction of inflight slots for short flows and preempts prefetch admission when shortflow backlog exceeds threshold
Limit prefetch and KV pre-warming for long-context requests under high contention (token-bucket with adaptive ceiling based on recent tail latency)
Add a graceful-degradation policy: when shortflow SLO threatened, route long-context requests to quantized/low-memory model variant or throttle their generation step rate
Implement fast-path KV cache read priority for queries tagged as shortflow to avoid eviction-induced stalls
Instrument new metrics and events for admission decisions, prefetch throttles, per-tenant reserved usage and degradation triggers
New unit and integration tests: deterministic simulator with mixed-length workload generator; chaos tests for KV eviction and host maintenance windows
Keep changes toggled behind runtime feature flag and rollout with canary gating and automatic rollback on SLO regressions
acceptance_criteria: Short-request (<=64 tokens) P99 reduced to baseline +/-10% under mixed workload in staging simulator
No regressions on throughput for Dedicated reserved capacity customers in canary tests
All new metrics emitted and dashboards created: tenant_short_preserve_util, tenant_prefetch_throttle, tenant_degradation_active
Automated canary job will abort rollout if shortflow P99 increases by >15% or KV eviction spikes by >30%
Documentation updated: scheduler admission config, per-tenant soft quota knobs, and runbook for rollback
Customer-facing incident notes drafted and communicated for impacted accounts
rollout_plan: 2) Staging cluster integration with real-model traces (feature-flag on) - target: 2026-03-13
3) Canary rollout in Hosted region 'us-west-2' for 5% traffic, monitor 6h - target: 2026-03-14
4) Gradual expansion to 30% then 100% in Hosted if canary stable, gate by canary-alerts
5) Coordinate Dedicated customer opt-in for controlled rollout and Private customers via patch notes and upgrade window
6) Post-rollout 72h observation window and follow-up SLO review
telemetry_and_alerts: Emit per-tenant metrics at 1s resolution: shortflow_p50/p95/p99, longflow_p50/p95/p99
Emit admission decision events: ADMIT/REJECT/PREEMPT with reason codes
Alert: tenant_shortflow_p99 > baseline*1.15 for 15m -> page oncall
Alert: KV_cache_eviction_rate spike > 2x baseline for 5m -> create incident
Dashboard: per-tenant heatmap of preserved-reservations vs usage
Trace sampling: when degradation triggers, capture end-to-end trace for 100% of affected requests for 30 minutes
